definition: OpenVINO is an open-source software toolkit developed by Intel for optimizing and deploying deep learning models.
details: It supports several popular model formats and workloads, including large language models, computer vision, generative AI, speech processing, and robot-policy deployment. OpenVINO is optimized for Intel hardware, but offers support for ARM/ARM64 processors. It sees use in AI Sound Processing drivers when tied with Intel's Gaussian & Neural Accelerator (GNA). Based in C++, it extends API support for C and Python, as well as Node.js. OpenVINO is cross-platform and free for use under Apache License 2.0.

explainer.lead: OpenVINO is Intel's open-source toolkit for optimizing and deploying deep learning models. It matters because it lets trained models run efficiently across Intel hardware and ARM processors.

tiers.eli5: It is a set of free tools that makes AI models run faster on certain computer chips, like tuning a car for a specific road.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers convert models into OpenVINO-supported formats and deploy them across vision, speech, generative AI and robot-policy workloads. A pitfall is assuming full speedup off Intel hardware, since ARM/ARM64 support is offered but optimization targets Intel.
tiers.paperLevel: It is an open-source deployment and optimization toolkit supporting C++, C, Python and Node.js APIs, cross-platform and licensed under Apache; it is tuned for Intel hardware with ARM/ARM64 support.

explainer.example: A computer vision model is optimized with OpenVINO and deployed on an Intel-based edge device, with the API called from Python.
